name: Sunflower

evidence.doc: FAO ECOCROP database (OpenCLIM copy), row: Helianthus annuus

frostTender.notes: The DAFF/ARC-GCI production guideline itself never mentions frost; it only says the crop is 'tolerant of both low and high temperatures but more tolerant to low temperatures' and germinates at soil temperatures from 5 degC. FAO ECOCROP's killing temperature (0 degC) is used here instead, since it is the only sourced frost data point found.

evidence.quote: In South Africa, sunflower is planted from the beginning of November until the end of December in the eastern areas and until mid-January in the western areas.
The total growing period (from seeding to harvesting) for sunflower ranges from 125 to 130 days.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Grain/seed maturity. Harvest should start once 80% of heads are brown, about 30-45 days after bloom, at ~35% seed moisture.

evidence.quote: Row width can range from 90 to 100 cm, however, wider rows can also be used, particularly to accommodate other managerial aspects of crop production.
The required spacing in the row is about 30 cm at seed depth of 5 to 8 cm.

inRowSpacingRangeCm.notes: Source gives a single value (~30cm), not a range.

evidence.quote: The required spacing in the row is about 30 cm at seed depth of 5 to 8 cm.

zoneNotes.highveld: North West (Dr Ruth Segomotsi Mompati, Dr Kenneth Kaunda, Ngaka Modiri Malema, Bojanala) and Free State (Motheo, Lejweleputswa, Mofutsanyane) districts are named as production areas.
zoneNotes.lowveld-bushveld: Limpopo (Capricorn, Waterberg) and Mpumalanga (Gert Sibande, Nkangala, Ehlanzeni) districts are named as production areas.

gaps: No DAFF/DALRRD-hosted sunflower guideline under nda.gov.za was found via Wayback in the initial CDX listing; the version used here ('Brochure Sunflower.pdf') was located under the dalrrd.gov.za Portals path.
No yield figure (t/ha) anywhere in the source.
No seed rate in kg/ha; only plant population (25 000-35 000 plants/ha) is given.
No named cultivars/varieties -- source only refers generically to 'disease resistant cultivars' and 'certified seeds'.
Frost sensitivity is not addressed by the primary source at all; frostTender is based on FAO ECOCROP's killing-temperature field instead, as noted above.
No winter-rainfall (Western Cape), all-year, or mild-frost specific sowing guidance -- only the summer-rainfall Nov-Dec(east)/mid-Jan(west) window is given.
'foodGroup' does not map cleanly onto this crop (an oilseed rather than a legume, leafy green, staple grain, etc.); left as null rather than forced into a wrong category.
summary: DAFF/ARC-GCI's 2009 Sunflower brochure gives a well-sourced sowing window, days-to-harvest, row/in-row spacing and sowing depth. It has no yield figure, no seed rate in kg/ha, and no named varieties, and never mentions frost (frostTender relies on FAO ECOCROP instead), so verdict is partial.
